cards.explanation: The answer is a great fish. Jonah 1:17 says the LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah. I think that's a strange kind of help, friends. But it's the one the text gives.

The answer is three days and three nights. Jonah 1:17 says Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the fish. That's a long stretch with no windows and no exits. I bet he counted every minute, but that's just my guess, friends.

The answer is that he prays to the LORD his God. From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD his God (Jonah 2:1). No crowd, no ship, no lifeboat, just Jonah talking to the LORD. Whatever else is going on in there, friends, the text puts the prayer first.

The answer is True. Jonah says, “In my distress I called to the LORD, and He answered me.” Then he says that from the belly of Sheol he called for help, and the LORD heard his voice (Jonah 2:2). He's telling the story of a prayer that got answered. That's a good thing to say from inside a fish, bakers.

The answer is the LORD. In his prayer, Jonah says to God, “For You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas…” (Jonah 2:3). He speaks directly to the LORD about it, friends. The sailors did throw him over (Jonah 1:15), but in his prayer, Jonah names the LORD.

The answer is that he will look once more toward God's holy temple. Jonah says, ‘I have been banished from Your sight; yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple.’ (Jonah 2:4). Notice that little word “yet,” bakers. Even with all that, he says what he will do.

The answer is that the LORD raised his life up from the pit. Jonah says the earth beneath him barred him in forever, and then comes the big “But.” “But You raised my life from the pit, O LORD my God!” (Jonah 2:6). He went down to the roots of the mountains, friends, and the LORD brought his life back up.

The word is remembered. Jonah says, “As my life was fading away, I remembered the LORD.” His life is fading, and the LORD is who he remembers. Then, friends, his prayer went up to the LORD's holy temple (Jonah 2:7).

The answer is False. Jonah says, “Those who cling to worthless idols forsake His loving devotion.” (Jonah 2:8). They hold on to idols and walk away from God's loving devotion, bakers. It's the opposite of holding on to it.

The word is thanksgiving. Jonah says, “But I, with the voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You.” (Jonah 2:9). He's still inside the fish when he says it, friends. The prayer started in distress, and here it's speaking thanks.

The word is salvation. Jonah finishes his prayer with, “Salvation is from the LORD!” (Jonah 2:9). It's a short line, but it lands hard, bakers. After everything he said about the deep, the last word is that the LORD is where salvation comes from.

The answer is that the fish vomits him onto dry land. The LORD commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land (Jonah 2:10). The fish doesn't act on its own here, friends, because the LORD gives the command. It isn't pretty, but Jonah ends up on solid ground. And this story isn't over.
